title: TTL lease lock with fencing tokens
source: Own model (traceforge/examples/lease_timed.rs). The scenario is the paused lease holder of M. Kleppmann, 'How to do distributed locking' (blog post, 2016), also the subject of the Jepsen etcd analyses: a client is granted a lease, pauses longer than the lease lives, and then writes with its stale token. The timing rule (the PAUSE bound) is derived in the header of the source file (lines 154 to 167); it does not come from a published table, and there are no external reference numbers.
property: At the storage, every applied write carries a token strictly greater than the last applied one, that is, a write of a superseded lease holder is never applied after a newer holder's write (one traceforge::assert in the Storage thread, line 441).
citable_note: The 2026-09-18 audit lists lease as citable with the wording 'matrix-verified', not 'exact'; the current source still passes its identical-program check (the mode is read only in build_config and in main; the only sleep is the pause under study, unconditional in both modes). Caveats: own model without external reference numbers; the boundary law is pinned by measurement at five settings (C=5, R=1), not proven; with fencing off the gain is the verdict only (the timed side needs 2.0 to 6.5 times the wall time of the baseline in every unfenced cell); with fencing on, 0 violations holds by construction and the result is the smaller exploration.
config_timed: lease_timed.rs build_config (lines 469 to 481): Config::builder().with_all_sends_lossy().with_progress_report(usize::MAX) (line 470); .with_keep_going_after_error(true) only when --keep-going is given (lines 471 to 476); then .with_timed(L, U, sd) with the resolved ticks (line 479). All else is the tool default (traceforge/src/lib.rs, ConfigBuilder::new, lines 347 to 386): FIFO channels (line 355), scheduling policy LTR (line 356), no symmetry reduction, no loss budget: every send may be dropped, without a bound. Exploration is sequential unless --parallel shared is given, which sets .with_parallel(true) (apply_parallel, lines 460 to 467): the shared work-queue pool, sized by MUST_PARALLEL_WORKERS or else by the number of CPUs the process may use (exec_pool.rs lines 379 to 385); the campaign scripts do not set the variable and pin every job to its cores, so the pool has one worker per core of the job. Timers of the program: the service waits TTL ticks for the holder's Release (WaitTime::Finite(ttl), lines 340 to 343) and client 0 sleeps PAUSE ticks after reading its Grant (lines 406 to 408); every other receive is a blocking timed receive.
config_baseline: The same builder without .with_timed (line 478: builder.build()): FIFO channels, scheduling policy LTR, every send lossy (with_all_sends_lossy at line 470 is set for both modes so that both check the same network), keep-going and --parallel exactly as on the timed side of the same cell. No clock: the tool ignores all timing information (lib.rs lines 549 to 551), so U, L, sd, TTL and PAUSE have no effect, the service's wait for the Release may end at any moment, and the baseline result depends only on C, R and fencing (measured: identical counts in settings A to E).
program_differs_between_modes: no: the mode is read only in build_config (lines 477 to 480) and in the dispatch of main; no protocol function takes it, and the only sleep (client 0's pause, lines 406 to 408) is unconditional
failing_tasks: Only the Storage thread asserts (line 441). It is the first thread the main closure spawns (line 523), so under keep-going every violating execution prints the line `task-1` (seen in local runs of the C=2 cells in both modes). Clients and the service contain only panics on messages the protocol cannot produce. Without --keep-going the first violation ends the process with exit code 101 and no summary line; in timed mode the message is 'assertion failed (certified timed counterexample; graph and witness above)' after a block 'Certified witness timeline'.

counters.meaning: STALE_APPLIED: raised just before the assertion when the storage is about to apply a write whose token is not above the last applied one (lines 437 to 441). The failed assertion ends the execution, so it counts each violating execution once. Equal to the tool's count in every sequential v9 run; in some shared-pool runs the tool's line count is lower by a few (see notes). Always 0 with fencing on.

STALE_REJECTED: writes the storage refused because their token was below the last applied one (fencing check, lines 431 to 435), summed over all explored executions, complete and blocked; several per execution are possible. Always 0 with fencing off. Not a violation: it shows that the stale write was reached and defused.

EXPIRED: waits of the lock service for a Release that ended without one (lines 349 to 354), summed over all explored executions; up to C*R per execution. Not a violation, and not evidence that the pause made a lease expire: every send may be dropped, and a dropped Grant or Release also ends in an expiry.

param_columns.meaning: number of clients competing for the lease (--clients); client 0 is the one that pauses, the others never pause
lease rounds (--rounds): in every round each client acquires the lease, writes once and releases; the threads live across rounds
on: the storage rejects a write whose token is below the last applied one (counted in stale); off: it applies every write, and the assertion is the mutual-exclusion property (--fencing)
upper bound of the transit time of every message (--u); like every tick value it matters on the timed side only
lower bound of the transit time, round(l-ratio * U) (--l-ratio)
storage delay: how long a message stays readable after it arrived, round(sd-ratio * U) (--sd-ratio)
lifetime of a lease = how long the lock service waits for the holder's Release before it grants the next client, round(ttl-ratio * U) (--ttl-ratio)
how long client 0 stalls between reading its Grant and sending its write, round(pause-ratio * U) (--pause-ratio)
derived, not a flag: TTL - 2(U - L + sd), the smallest PAUSE at which the unfenced protocol violates in timed mode; any PAUSE below it is safe

boundary_law: With fencing off, the timed side reports a violation exactly when PAUSE >= TTL - 2(U - L + sd) (all in ticks), at every round count R; with fencing on there is no boundary. Origin: the header of lease_timed.rs (lines 154 to 167): the write of the paused holder can still be read at the storage up to grant_send + PAUSE + 2(U + sd), the next holder's write cannot be read before grant_send + TTL + 2L, and the violation is realizable exactly when the first reaches the second (equality counts as a violation). The source calls the rule matrix-verified, for R in {1,2}, U in {1,2}, L in {0,U}, sd in {0,1}. Checked in v9 (commit b67ccf7, C=5, R=1, exhaustive runs, timed side): in each of the five settings 0 violating executions at PAUSE = bound - 1 and above 0 at PAUSE = bound. A: bound 4, PAUSE 3 safe (0), PAUSE 4 violating (48240). B: bound 8, PAUSE 7 safe (0), PAUSE 8 violating (41760). C: bound 6, PAUSE 5 safe (0), PAUSE 6 violating (34416). D: bound 2, PAUSE 1 safe (0), PAUSE 2 violating (48240). E: bound 10, PAUSE 9 safe (0), PAUSE 10 violating (29160). Also at setting A: without keep-going the timed side explores everything at PAUSE 3 (C=4, exit code 0) and stops with a certified counterexample at PAUSE 4 (C=6, exit code 101); the safe side (PAUSE 3) has 0 violations at every size measured: C=2 R=1, C=2 R=3, C=2 R=4, C=2 R=5, C=2 R=6, C=3 R=1, C=3 R=2, C=4 R=1, C=4 R=2, C=5 R=1 in v9, C=3 R=3, C=6 R=1 in v8 only so far. Not measured in this campaign: pauses further away from the bound, the violating side with R >= 2, settings B, C, D with fencing on, and TTL varied independently of U.

glossary.meaning: the integer time unit of the timed mode; U, L, sd, TTL, PAUSE and the bound are all in ticks. The ratio flags are multiplied by U and rounded (lease_timed.rs lines 270 to 285)

the right to write to the storage, granted to one client at a time by the lock service; it lives TTL ticks: if no Release of the holder arrives within TTL after the Grant was sent, the service treats the lease as expired and grants the next client
the number issued with each Grant, increasing by one per grant across all rounds; a client attaches its token to its write

fenced: the storage compares the token of each write with the last applied one and rejects a smaller one, which makes the protocol safe without any timing assumption. Unfenced: the storage applies every write, and safety depends on PAUSE against TTL
client 0 stalls for PAUSE ticks (a garbage-collection pause or scheduling stall) after reading its Grant and before it writes; the phenomenon under study and the only sleep in the program

glossary.term: PAUSE bound ('bnd' in the cell names)
glossary.meaning: TTL - 2(U - L + sd): the unfenced protocol is safe for PAUSE < bound and violating for PAUSE >= bound. 'bnd-1' in a cell name is the largest safe pause, 'bnd' the smallest violating one

glossary.term: setting A to E (the regime letter)
glossary.meaning: the five network timing settings. A: U=2, L=0, sd=1, TTL=10 (bound 4). B: U=2, L=2, sd=1, TTL=10 (bound 8). C: U=2, L=0, sd=0, TTL=10 (bound 6). D: U=1, L=0, sd=1, TTL=6 (bound 2). E: U=2, L=2, sd=0, TTL=10 (bound 10)
-safe: unfenced, PAUSE = bound - 1. -viol: unfenced, PAUSE = bound. -ctrl: fenced, PAUSE = bound. So the Fencing column is off for -safe and -viol and on for -ctrl
a write whose token is below the last applied one: its sender was superseded by a newer holder. Applied (a violation) when unfenced, rejected and counted in stale when fenced
violating executions as counted by the program itself, one per execution in which the storage was about to apply a stale write
stale writes rejected by the fencing check, counted as events over all explored executions; above 0 means the dangerous interleaving was explored and defused
waits for a Release that ran out, counted as events over all explored executions; a lost Grant or Release expires a lease too, so this is not a measure of the pause
further event counts printed by the example: Grants sent, Releases received in time, writes applied; all summed over complete and blocked executions

an execution in which some thread waits forever for a message that was dropped or is no longer readable (a client for its RoundStart, Grant or WriteAck, the service for an Acquire, the storage for a write), or, under keep-going, in which the assertion failed. Every send can be dropped, so most explored executions are blocked

glossary.term: headline, clients ladder, rounds ladder, ceiling
glossary.meaning: roles of the cells: the headline cells are C=5 and C=6 with R=1; the clients ladder raises C with R=1; the rounds ladder raises R at C=2, 3, 4; the ceiling cells are the largest sizes tried (C=7 R=1, C=2 R=6, C=3 R=3, C=4 R=2)

Notes against source. (1) The memory note p1_lease_swim_examples.md calls the example untracked on branch p1-examples and not wired into any sweep: outdated, the file is committed and is the lease family of v8 and v9. (2) The same note and the 2026-09-18 audit call the service's wait for the Release an unvalidated timeout (expired above 0 even at TTL=100 with no pause). An expiry therefore needs no pause at all (a dropped Grant or Release is enough; a local run at TTL=100, PAUSE=0 still prints expired above 0), so expired above 0 remains no evidence that the pause-induced expiry was explored. (5) The source header (lines 10, 137) and a comment in build_config (line 473) name the baseline with a word this workbook avoids; the metadata says baseline throughout.
